stories.title: Who's ducking in Peyton's back seat?
stories.teaser: Peyton Pastel's car-deal tryout photo has a stranger hiding in the back seat. Peyton says "edit it out". Astoria says "zoom in".

pieces.text: Jojo, wiping the steamer: "Peyton zoomed in on her own photo right here, screamed, and spilled a lavender latte. The stowaway's scarf was her exact pink. Ask at Thread Count who sold it."
Two clerks folding sweaters: "Somebody bought our last scarf in Peyton Pink, paid in quarters, and asked if it 'reads famous in the background'. Then she asked for directions to the car lot."
A salesman to his manager: "The demo car's back seat had a phone tripod, a granola bar and a ring light. Nobody here owns a ring light. She got in Tuesday and got out Thursday."
Inez, scrolling her camera: "Third proposal shoot this week with the same girl in a pink scarf waving in the background. I said 'excuse me'. She said 'tag me'. She's at the movies tonight, bragging."
Row F, during the trailers: "That's me in Peyton's back seat. Forty-one new followers. Next week I'm going to be in the back of something bigger." Her friend: "Tiff, please sit down."

tea.headline: Tiff has been living in the background of Peyton's car deal
tea.body: The mystery passenger in Peyton Pastel's car-deal photo is Tiff, "basically an influencer", who bought a scarf in Peyton Pink with quarters, moved into a demo car at Boulevard Motors for two days, and has photobombed three proposals at Gantry Plaza while she was at it. Forty-one new followers, most of them still bots. Peyton's team wants her edited out. The car company wants her in the next ad. And to everyone asking: no, a girl who lived in a car lot this week was not in anybody else's back seat on Saturday. Lola, out.

stories.title: The cannoli on Sgt. Bev's desk
stories.teaser: Every morning at seven, one cannoli appears on the 114½ Precinct's front desk. No note. No witnesses. One very annoyed sergeant.

pieces.text: Sgt. Bev, chewing: "Fourth cannoli this week. I'm a sergeant, hon. I'll find him. The box says Ditmars Deli, so go lean on Sal. Lean hard. Not too hard."
Sal, slicing: "I don't sell cannoli. I sell the box. Big guy buys an empty box every morning at six-thirty, fills it somewhere else. The Neon Spoon makes them. I'm not jealous."
A waitress at the counter: "Big guy in a fire jacket orders one cannoli to go every morning and writes a speech on the napkin. He's never finished the speech. Ask the firehouse who he is."
Captain Rosa, arms crossed: "Lenny's been 'checking a hydrant' by the precinct every morning at seven. There's no hydrant by the precinct. Gus sees him practicing. Ask Gus."

Gus, from his bench: "Every evening, same fella. 'Bev, would you like… a cannoli.' Then he panics and eats the cannoli. Two weeks. That's a lot of cannoli. I haven't seen courage like this since 1987."

tea.headline: The firehouse is courting the precinct, one cannoli at a time
tea.body: Astoria's sweetest stakeout is over. Firefighter Lenny of Engine 7 has been buying an empty box at Ditmars Deli, filling it at The Neon Spoon and "checking a hydrant that doesn't exist" outside the 114½ Precinct at seven every morning. Every evening he rehearses his big line on Gus's bench, then eats the evidence. Sgt. Bev has known since day two; she's a sergeant. She's just waiting for him to finish the speech. Lola's prediction: by Friday it's two cannoli on that desk and one very red firefighter.

stories.title: Tillwater's ribbon to nowhere
stories.teaser: Councilmember Barb Tillwater cut the ribbon on Astoria's "new elevator". Commuters pressed the button. It's a closet.

pieces.text: Mr. Penwright, lowering his voice: "The councilmember borrowed our ceremonial scissors. We have one pair. She returned them with a bit of ribbon and said 'Astoria Blvd, big day.' Go see."
On the platform: "The new elevator door opens onto a mop and two buckets. She pressed 'lobby'. The mop did not move." "Who even told her there was an elevator?"
Somebody at a hot desk, on speaker: "The press release said 'Astoria's newest elevator, ribbon cutting Monday'. City Hall didn't write it. It came from a domain name. Of course it did."
At the best table: "My stealth startup just got a ribbon cutting from City Hall, guys. Elevator Pitch Night. Two Bros is catering. Officially a city landmark." It is a closet, Chad.

Both brothers behind the counter: "She ordered a celebration pie for the elevator! Then she found out! Then she ordered ANOTHER pie and called the closet 'Astoria's first pitch room'! She's committed!"

tea.headline: City Hall cut a ribbon on Chad Kensington's pitch-night closet
tea.body: Chad Kensington, CEO of a stealth startup (a domain name), sent City Hall a press release for "Astoria's newest elevator": his Elevator Pitch Night, held in a janitor's closet at Astoria Blvd station. Councilmember Barb Tillwater, who types fast and proofreads never, read faster. She borrowed the library's only ceremonial scissors, cut the ribbon, pressed "lobby" and met a mop. Rather than back down, she ordered a second pie and declared the closet "Astoria's first pitch room". The mop has not been consulted. Lola, out.

stories.title: Chase Clout's missing 47 minutes
stories.teaser: Chase Clout's stream went dark for 47 minutes, his first break in three years. Chat has theories. Astoria has receipts.

pieces.text: Pixel, staring at a chair: "First Saturday in three years he wasn't in that chair. It's still warm. Emotionally. Rocco at Hellgate says he saw him outside without a phone. I don't believe it."

Rocco, at the rope: "Chase Clout. No phone, no headset, standing on the sidewalk staring at a tree like it was a new map. Then he asked me where you buy 'quiet'. I said the grocery store. I was joking."
Two cashiers: "He bought a candle called Unplugged Meadow and asked if outside has a mute button. Then he asked for directions to the lounge, 'somewhere dark where nobody says chat'."
A man in a booth, on the phone: "He's not banned, he's resting. Is resting a thing? Can we sell resting? Fine, sign him up for the college class. Under a fake name. C. Lout."

Two students in the hallway: "Beginners' Meditation had a new guy, 'C. Lout'. He said 'chat, breathe in' at minute two and fell asleep at minute three. Snored for forty-four minutes. Best class we've had."

tea.headline: Chase Clout's mystery blackout was a nap in a meditation class
tea.body: The 47 minutes that broke the internet: Chase Clout logged off, bought a candle called Unplugged Meadow, let his manager sign him up for Beginners' Meditation at Astoria Community College as "C. Lout", said "chat, breathe in" and slept for forty-four minutes. His first rest in three years. He woke up refreshed and announced a fourteen-hour meditation stream, which rather misses the point. And no, a man snoring on a yoga mat was not anybody's mystery date. Lola, out.
